allow.why: The one redirect rule of the old addresses: every /ar address answers 308 to the same path under /en (plan 30 §7.1). It has to name the old prefix.
Reads a leading /ar of a ?next= value (a bookmark or an old sign-in redirect) as /en before the usual checks (plan 30 §7.1). It has to name the old prefix.
Tests of that rule: they need the old /ar addresses as input.
A stored notification link that still starts with /ar leads to /en (plan 30 §7.1). It has to name the old prefix.
Tests of that rule: they need the old /ar links as input.
Tries every old /ar address against the build: the 308 to /en, the token links and the two seeded old slugs.
Group C: IMEI digits typed on an Arabic keyboard (Arabic-Indic and Persian) are read as Latin digits; the test needs those digits.
Group C: a quantity typed with Arabic-Indic or Persian digits is read; the test needs those digits.
Group C: an amount typed with Arabic-Indic digits and the Arabic decimal mark is read; the test needs them.
Group C: a typed quantity or IMEI list with Arabic-Indic digits is read; the test needs those digits.
Group C: an IMEI typed with Arabic-Indic digits in the search box is recognised; the test needs those digits.
Group C: a search typed in Arabic passes through the text clean-up unchanged; the test needs an Arabic query.
Group C: Arabic text in a WhatsApp link is percent-encoded and a referral code in Arabic is refused; the tests need Arabic samples.
Group C: a ticket message typed in Arabic is shown as typed, in a box with dir="auto"; the test needs an Arabic body.
Group C (plan 30 §9.5): ticket text, file names, API values, initials and the input-method Enter for text typed in Arabic; the samples are Arabic.
Group C: a quantity typed with an Arabic-Indic digit is read in the order form.

keep.why: A ticket message is text a person typed, and may be Arabic: it keeps its own direction (group C, decision 039).
A file name is chosen by a person and may be Arabic: it keeps its own direction (group C).
A value of the API (or a supplier's own words) is isolated from the sentence around it (group C).
The initial of a name typed in any script, Arabic included, is its first character, not its first UTF-16 unit (group C).
An IMEI typed on an Arabic keyboard (Arabic-Indic and Persian digits) is read as Latin digits (group C).
A quantity typed on an Arabic keyboard is read (group C).
An amount typed on an Arabic keyboard is read (group C).
The Enter that confirms an input method's text (Arabic, Chinese, Japanese) does not send a ticket reply (group C).
